text:
Russia’s top diplomat accused Paris of directly taking part in the Ukraine war following a report that French troops are in the eastern European country carrying out noncombatant operations.
“We conveyed our concern through available channels, warning the relevant countries that this is no longer support for Ukraine, but direct participation in the war,” Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov told reporters Tuesday at the East Asia Summit in Manila, adding that French troops were also “assisting in goal setting, providing satellite data and much more.”
Lavrov’s comments come a day after Radio France Internationale revealed Paris had kept troops in Ukraine for several months to provide training and equipment maintenance under the “Volia mission.” The troops, who are in the French military detachment in Poland, have been involved in the operation in Ukraine since at least summer 2026, RFI reported.
Since the Kremlin launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, Russian officials have periodically warned Europe against putting troops into the country, as Moscow looks to deter the continent from participating in Ukraine’s resistance with active soldiers.
The Elysée Palace did not immediately respond to POLITICO’s request for comment.
French Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot pledged to fight “tooth and nail” for European security during Monday’s meeting of EU foreign ministers in Brussels, following the announcement that Paris would represent Europe in Ukraine peace talks as part of the “E5,” alongside Germany, Italy, Poland and the U.K.
In Manila, Lavrov declined to expand on the upcoming trilateral meeting between U.S. President Donald Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin, taking place in Shenzhen in southeastern China on Thursday.
“It is broadly clear what the leaders will discuss. They will have an opportunity for a free exchange of views. Be patient. There is very little time left to wait,” Lavrov told reporters.
